items.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025
items.q: When you were working with Gamble and Huff and Thom Bell... I also think Gamble, Huff and Bell... I would wait for Tommy Bell to smile or Gamble & Huff to say damn that's nice

ctx.x: I don't want to make too much out of this but it seems to me when you were making this decision at 17 according to your promo here, that you had one foot in the white world of music and you had another in the black world of music. Were you aware of that? Was that partly your decision to go — to leave Curtis and go in this other direction?

Well you know at that moment it was the hippie days so I was playing in a few bands. The bands were based on blues. Blues obviously the derivative of blues is black music, the church the old work songs, every — all that. You know? So yeah I was fascinated. I was also fascinated by popular music in general. But in Philadelphia the people that were really adept that I met were people like Leon Huff and people like, you know they were Tommy Bell and they were really crazily talented people that weren't talented like…
